q4.answer: Payment charges only when it consumes an InventoryReserved event in the payment group. Inventory writes that event only in the same transaction as a stock reservation, and Payment ignores InventoryRejected, so no reserved stock means no charge.

q5.answer: Each service writes its result event to its own outbox in the same transaction as its state change, and the relay publishes it. If a service crashes after committing but before the relay publishes, the outbox row is still unsent, so the relay publishes it on a later poll.

q6.answer: Each consumer checks its processed_events table for the eventId and, if it is present, acknowledges the message and does nothing. The effect and the processed_events row commit in one transaction, so a duplicate cannot apply twice. At Order Service, the conditional update WHERE status = PENDING also makes a second cancelling event a no-op.

q7.answer: Payment commits a CHARGING row before calling the card provider and sends the idempotency key orderId on every attempt. The provider returns the first result for that key without charging again, so the redelivered message cannot create a second charge, and Payment then commits the result.

q9.answer: The PaymentDeclined event, delivered to the inventory group, causes the release. Inventory is the only service that releases it, changing the reservation from RESERVED to RELEASED in one transaction that also records the eventId. Publish order guarantees it always sees InventoryReserved first, so it never releases a reservation it did not make.

q10.answer: Order Service consumes PaymentCaptured, PaymentDeclined and InventoryRejected in the order group. In one transaction it runs a conditional update WHERE status = PENDING, setting CONFIRMED on PaymentCaptured or CANCELLED on the other two, records the eventId, and writes OrderConfirmed or OrderCancelled to its outbox. If the update matches no row, the order already has a final status and nothing else happens.

q11.answer: The customer email is triggered by OrderConfirmed or OrderCancelled in the notification group, so email only follows a final status. A failed send never changes the order status; Notification records SENDING, then FAILED, retries, and then uses the DLQ and paging path. Whether an email failure should page on-call or only raise a ticket is still an open question, so that part is not decided.
